title: Agent structures repeated, and in a harder setting
what: The agent-structure comparison (single plan, repeated planning up to three turns, planner plus challenger) had one run per structure and family on a five-drawing workspace. This record repeats it three times per case, and adds a harder setting: the six test families' thirty base drawings indexed together (a family of the same kind sits beside the asked one), twelve candidates returned instead of six, and a second query per family asking for the other material (AL6061). The expected verdict of every indexed drawing is computed from the gold facts (kind, value, material) and the free rules path reproduces all of them (integration test). Verdicts come from the deterministic verifier; the model chooses which lookups to make and when to stop. Harness: src/fitwitness/evaluation/agent_trajectory.py (--repeats, --workspace, --materials, --top-k), manual workflow agent-trajectory.yml.
why_gpt_5_mini: the Anthropic account balance was empty on 2026-10-30, so the Claude repeat stopped after one repeat of two structures; the OpenAI adapter had never run this graph and needed a fix first (function calling for the plan schema, minimal reasoning for the reasoning model)

runs.purpose: the original protocol repeated three times with Claude Haiku 4.5
runs.result: interrupted by an empty Anthropic balance (HTTP 400 'credit balance is too low'): repeat 0 of single plan finished 6/6 families with all 30 verdicts right, repeat 0 of repeated planning 6/6 with 30/30, repeat 0 of planner+challenger finished one family (5/5), then one call failed mid-run and the next run's first call was rejected, which stopped the batch; 39 runs were skipped. Model rows cost 0.07695 USD (the ledger counts 0.114548 because it keeps the reservation of the call cut off mid-flight). Too few runs to say anything about repeats.

one family: the first call of every structure was rejected by OpenAI (HTTP 400, invalid schema for response_format 'SearchPlan': additionalProperties must be false). The OpenAI adapter had never run the drawing graph. 0.0054 USD kept as a reservation.
one family after the adapter asked OpenAI for function calling: all three structures 5/5 ($0.0057). Not part of the numbers below.

runs.purpose: the original protocol repeated three times

findings: Easy setting, gpt-5-mini, three repeats: all 54 runs (18 per structure) finished with every verdict right and no invariant violation. All three structures are at the ceiling, so the setting cannot rank them. 4 plans needed one schema repair.

Hard setting: none of the three structures is near the ceiling. Runs with every verdict right: single plan 0 of 36, repeated planning 6 of 36, planner plus challenger 7 of 36. Verdict accuracy over all runs 54.8%, 64.1%, 61.6%; over the runs that finished 67.3%, 75.7%, 80.2%. The two readings order the multi-turn structures differently because the challenger runs also failed more often (9 of 36 against 6 and 7), so the data do not rank repeated planning against planner plus challenger.

Every wrong verdict is a drawing nobody looked up (not_inspected 112, 89, 64) or a run that ended before its verdicts (run_incomplete 78, 66, 98); inspected_wrong is 0 in all 108 runs. The model never misjudged a drawing it had inspected; it stopped before it had inspected them all (coverage before the first verdict 54%, 57%, 50%).

The single plan cannot cover twelve candidates by construction: a plan holds at most 8 operations, one lookup each, so it can inspect 8 of 12 (the nine tool calls are the search and eight lookups). Its 0 of 36 is the harness's shape, not a finding about the model; the two multi-turn structures have the turns to cover all twelve and still stopped early in most runs (stop reason plan_stop 24 and 17 times).
Runs ended in failure on a plan that did not fit the schema even after the one repair: 7, 6 and 9 of 36 (ValueError: model output failed schema validation). In the easy setting none failed.

The same case gave different verdicts across its three repeats in 5, 10 and 8 of 12 cases; no case was right in all three repeats under the single plan or repeated planning, and one under planner plus challenger (pass^3 0, 0, 0.083).
limitations: One model (gpt-5-mini, minimal reasoning) in the repeated runs; the Claude Haiku 4.5 repeat was cut off by an empty balance after one repeat of two structures. Nothing here says how Claude behaves in the harder setting, and earlier Claude single runs (agent-trajectory.json) are not comparable with these.

Twelve cases (six families x two materials) times three repeats: the repeats of a case are not independent, so counts of runs overstate how much was observed; 12 cases cannot rank two structures that differ by one or two cases.

The harder setting is hard by the harness's limits (at most 8 operations per plan, 16 tool calls, 4 model calls, 12 candidates), not by the drawings. The single plan's ceiling of 8 of 12 is one of them.

Retrieval is the same for every structure (drawing-number and BM25 channels, 12 candidates returned, all of the family's own drawings among them in every case); semantic and image channels are not part of this measurement.
Synthetic drawings. The verdicts are the deterministic verifier's; a failure here is a path failure, not a misjudgement.
Run costs are priced from third-party listings entered by hand; the OpenAI invoice is the truth.
